note: DESIGN NOTES — the floor, the derived verdict, and the cost this node pays elsewhere (12/22, gate-cadence §7). (1) THE FLOOR IS ONE VALUE. `closeBlocker(id)` = `closeEvidenceBlocker` + the v18 conclusion gate (every AC claimed-or-transferred, every claim's check resolving, none resting on a failed run). Read by FOUR paths now: `submit! confirm` (refuses the submission — zero writes, no rejection burned), the `gate!` accept auto-close, `brief`, and the frame's gate step. (2) WHERE IT IS READ INSIDE `gateImpl`, AND WHY THAT PLACEMENT IS THE HALF ACCEPT'S (12/12): after the transfer the SAME act writes. The predicate is asked of the record the act has already written, so a half accept still closes — one predicate, one path, no exception. Hoisting it before the try (the first cut) made every half accept stop at `no-structured-conclusion`; that is the regression the placement fixes. (3) THE FRAME COULD NOT SUBMIT CONFIRM BEFORE THE RECORD COULD CLOSE — a deliberate behaviour change, and the tests were REFRAMED, not weakened: run 1 now ends `blocked-waiting` with the exit gate UNOPENED (`gateState(confirm) === 'none'`), and the concluding run is where the gate is submitted, decided and closed. A fixture whose evidence carried no claims and no captured pass was a record `complete!` itself would refuse — the exact divergence AC-1 closes. (4) ABSENCE IS A NOTICE, NEVER A PROBLEM. The worker's absence and its `uncertain` hand-off ride `FrameResult.notices` (new field), so no run can read as failed for an outage; the floor's blocker rides the `waiting` note. (5) THE COST, NAMED RATHER THAN BURIED — the card's half accept is now unreachable from the page. `POST /api/transfer` (12/13 AC-5) serves a gate that is IN HAND, and a live confirm submission now presupposes a record that could close (AC-1). So the case that route was built for — an AC the task did NOT meet, moved at the accept — cannot be submitted any more: `submit! confirm` refuses it, and by the time the transfer is written the AC must already be claimed (and 12/12's claim-wins rule then reads the move as a claim). The half accept itself is NOT lost: the CLI's one `gate! confirm accept <why> --transfer` gesture auto-submits and closes in the same act. The 12/13 e2e fixture was reframed onto the reachable state with this cost written into the test that asserts it. If the page is to keep the affordance, the follow-up is a route that records the move BEFORE the submission — the operator's call, and it belongs to the UI journey, not to this node. (6) TWO MEASURED CONSEQUENCES IN THE SUITE: a confirm submission now calls the provider, so e2e tests that drive a lifecycle are spawn-bound plus a bounded 3-retry outage (~3.7s) — the budget is explicit on those tests, the assertions unchanged; and the README command table was regenerated from `ann commands`, which is the derived source.
